files.purpose: Declares LinkParagraphView, the NSViewRepresentable that renders a markdown paragraph containing links as a selectable, non-editable NSTextView (LinkTextView) so links show the native pointing hand and prose the I-beam, and its static attributed(source:pointSize:dimmed:streaming:mentions:targets:) builder that turns RichLink.prettyAttributed runs into an NSAttributedString with a per-size font cache (base, bold, font-manager italic, monospaced at max(9, pointSize - 1)), 14x14 favicon attachments from FaviconCache.cached(host:), dimmed labelColor at alpha 0.7 and Hydra head mentions (tinted dragon glyph at (pointSize * 1.25).rounded(), a space, the bold name in the persona colour, carrying the custom key "droppycode.hydraHead" rather than .link). LinkTextView owns its own NSTextStorage/NSLayoutManager/NSTextContainer, drops every tracking area and cursor rect, does its own link and head-mention hit testing, intercepts right-click/control-click to show LinkPopover and left-click on a head to call onOpenHead, measures height once per width and defers re-measurement during live resize. The file also declares MergeRequestTarget and its environment key, the hydraHead attribute key, and (new at B3) MarkdownLinkOpener, which opens scheme-less absolute-path links as local files, stripping a trailing :line suffix when only the file without it exists.

side_effects: Clicking a link opens it through MarkdownLinkOpener.open: NSWorkspace.shared.open(url) for any URL with a scheme, host, query or fragment or whose path does not start with "/"; otherwise NSWorkspace.shared.open(URL(fileURLWithPath: path)) on the local path (B3 :226-245)
MarkdownLinkOpener reads the file system (fileExists) to decide whether to strip a trailing ":<line>"
A left click on a head mention calls onOpenHead(url) and swallows the event (:444-451)
A right-click or control-click on a link shows LinkPopover.shared under the link's glyph bounds (:453-471)
render(_:) resets linkTextAttributes to the accent, no underline, pointing-hand cursor on every call (:485-489)
platform_assumptions: AppKit NSTextView with a TextKit 1 NSLayoutManager/NSTextContainer stack owned by the view
NSWorkspace.shared.open for both web URLs and file URLs (default handler)
POSIX absolute paths: MarkdownLinkOpener only treats a URL whose path begins with "/" as a local file, and a trailing ":<positive Int>" as a line suffix
No tracking areas or cursor rects; the enclosing SwiftUI hover (LinkHoverModifier) sets the cursor
Right-click and control-click routing via rightMouseDown(with:) and menu(for:)
ui_elements: Link paragraph text view: selectable, non-editable, no background, links in Chrome.accentNSColor with underlineStyle 0 and NSCursor.pointingHand
Favicon attachment 14x14 at y = base.descender + 1 followed by one space before a link
Head mention chip: tinted dragon glyph at (base.pointSize * 1.25).rounded(), a space, bold persona name in the persona colour; hydraHead attribute when a target exists
feature_notes: B2->B3 (commit ff5032673 'Fix opening local file links in chat'): Coordinator.textView(_:clickedOnLink:at:) (:90-100) now calls MarkdownLinkOpener.open(url) at :92 and :96 instead of NSWorkspace.shared.open(url). Observable change: a markdown link whose target is a bare absolute path (no scheme, host, query or fragment, path starting with "/") now opens that local file in its default application via a file URL; before B3 it was handed to NSWorkspace as a scheme-less URL.

New enum MarkdownLinkOpener (:226-245): guard url.scheme == nil, url.host == nil, url.query == nil, url.fragment == nil, url.path.hasPrefix("/") else NSWorkspace.shared.open(url). Otherwise path = url.path; if nothing exists at path, and the text after path's last ":" parses as an Int > 0, and the part before that colon exists and is not a directory, the ":<line>" suffix is dropped; then NSWorkspace.shared.open(URL(fileURLWithPath: path)). The line number is discarded, not used to position an editor. Only the last colon is examined, so "file.swift:12:5" is not stripped; ":0" and negative numbers are not stripped; a path that exists as given is opened as is.

Refactor (commit d70cff8fe): appendProse's inline longest-first, word-bounded scan (B2 :187, :189-190, :199-219, :240-241) is replaced by `for match in MentionScanner.matches(in: string, candidates: mentions, name: \.name)` (B3 :197-220). Compared line by line with MentionScanner.swift:7-32: same sort predicate (name.count descending), same hasPrefix test, same before/after checks (!isLetter && !isNumber, start/end of string accepted), same advance past the name. No observable change; the emitted runs (flush, attachment, hydraHead attributes, space, name) are unchanged, only shifted up 20 lines (B2 :220-238 -> B3 :200-218).

Cross-file context (not this bundle): the same commit changed MarkdownView.swift so InlineText takes the LinkParagraphView path when RichLink.containsLinks(in:streaming:) is true rather than only when a link has a host, so host-less local file links now reach this view and its opener.
unresolved_questions: UNRESOLVED: On Windows, agent-written local paths are drive-letter forms (C:\..., C:/...) that URL(string:) would parse with a one-letter scheme or reject, so an exact-parity guard (path must start with "/" and scheme must be nil) would never treat them as local files. Whether the port should recognise drive-letter paths is a platform-adaptation decision for the owner; nothing in the pinned source covers it.
UNRESOLVED: What URL(fileURLWithPath:) of a POSIX path such as "/Users/x/a.swift" should map to on Windows (for example the current drive's root) is not defined by the source.
UNRESOLVED: The macOS runtime result of NSWorkspace.shared.open on a file URL that does not exist (silent false or an alert) was not observed; the source ignores the return value.

files.purpose: Declares LinkPopover, the single shared transient NSPopover that a right-click or control-click on a chat link opens in place of the system text menu, anchored below the link's own glyph rect (preferredEdge .minY in the flipped text view), measured from an NSHostingView with a 220x110 fallback, and closed by Escape through a local keyDown monitor on key code 53 that is removed on close and in popoverDidClose. Its private SwiftUI content, LinkPopoverContent, is a 220-point-wide, 6-point-padded column of house PopoverItem rows: an optional "Merge <label>" row (semibold "Merge", the forge favicon or the arrow.triangle.merge symbol) plus a divider when the chat supplied a MergeRequestTarget, then "Open Link" (safari symbol) and "Copy Link" (link symbol, writes url.absoluteString to the general pasteboard). At B3 the Open Link row goes through MarkdownLinkOpener.open(url), so a local absolute-path link opens the file rather than being handed to NSWorkspace as-is.

feature_notes: B2->B3 (commit ff5032673): the only change is :89, `NSWorkspace.shared.open(url)` -> `MarkdownLinkOpener.open(url)` inside the "Open Link" row. Labels, symbols, layout, Merge and Copy Link are unchanged, and no line shifted (108 lines at both baselines).

Observable effect: choosing Open Link on a scheme-less absolute-path link now opens the local file in its default application (dropping a trailing :<line> when only the file without it exists) instead of handing a scheme-less URL to NSWorkspace; every other link behaves exactly as at B2.
The row keeps the "safari" symbol and the label "Open Link" for local file links; no label change accompanies the behaviour change.
unresolved_questions: UNRESOLVED (shared with LinkParagraphView.swift): whether the Windows port's Open Link should also treat drive-letter paths as local files; exact parity recognises only "/"-prefixed, scheme-less URLs.

files.purpose: Declares ProseRunView, the SwiftUI view a finished reply uses to render a run of consecutive paragraphs, headings, lists and quotes as one selectable LinkTextView (so selection and links span the whole run), reading point size, dimming, Hydra mention personas and targets and openURL from the environment, rounding the size to half points ((pointSize * 2).rounded() / 2), fetching link assets for the run's joined sources in a task keyed by RichLink.linkAssetKey, and (at B3) attaching the shared LinkHoverModifier for the pointing hand and the Hydra head hover card. Its ProseRunRepresentable builds one NSAttributedString from the blocks, reusing LinkParagraphView.attributed for each line: paragraphs with indent and paragraphSpacing, headings at 1.35/1.2/1.08 times the size with non-bold non-mono runs set semibold and spacing before 6 or 2, list items with "☑"/"☐", "n." or "•"/"◦" markers and a tab stop at indent + 18, quotes at indent + 14 forced dimmed, code/table/rule dropped, and a newline between blocks. It shares LinkParagraphView.Coordinator for its rebuild check and keeps onOpenHead and mergeTarget fresh on every update.

Ordinary link clicks in a prose run reach LinkParagraphView.Coordinator (shared via makeCoordinator), so they now go through MarkdownLinkOpener as a consequence of the LinkParagraphView.swift change.
